latency.timing_boundary: one prepared PostgreSQL generation/fetch of all root-first bytea columns, OCPB decode, and complete owned materialization of every node including exact violations and the typed Q6 label
latency.correctness_boundary: outside the clock: external-ID conversion, duplicate-preserving canonical row sorting, compact JSON, SHA-256, every-node manifest comparison, and independent Q6 child-duration validation
latency.query_protocol: exact upstream OCPQ primary protocol: zero warmups and ten direct measured evaluations per Q1-Q7
latency.process_scope: one selected query in a fresh candidate process; publication aggregation requires one fresh container for each Q1-Q7
latency.p50_estimator: conventional median; the middle two samples are averaged for the even ten-run sample
latency.p95_estimator: nearest-rank p95; with ten measured runs this is the maximum sample

memory.measurement_boundary: fresh Linux process: baseline after connection, provenance query, and one prepared statement; then one PostgreSQL generation/fetch, every OCPB node decode, and complete owned-tree materialization; RSS and VmHWM sampled while the entire tree remains live and before external-ID maps or canonicalization are loaded
memory.correctness_boundary: after the memory sample, load external-ID maps and require duplicate-preserving canonical JSON SHA-256 and manifest parity for every node, including exact violations and Q6 typed label/child-derived duration

resources.storage_boundary: untimed serving footprint from pg_total_relation_size/pg_indexes_size for every ocpm schema serving relation, with relation-level evidence
resources.concurrency_boundary: per-client persistent PostgreSQL connection and prepared Q1-Q7 tree set; every timed request includes PostgreSQL generation/fetch, decode of every OCPB node, and complete owned-tree materialization; canonicalization is excluded
resources.concurrency_protocol: fixed 1/4/8/16 clients, three epochs per level, each epoch at least five seconds and at least 32 requests per client; requests rotate Q1-Q7; every client performs exact every-node canonical parity for Q1-Q7 both before and after every timed epoch
resources.concurrency_raw_evidence: positive integer nanosecond latency for every request, grouped by client ID in request order; zero-based array index is the client request ID and query=Q1..Q7[(client_id+request_id)%7]
resources.correctness_boundary: duplicate-preserving external-ID canonical JSON, exact violation reasons, typed Q6 label and child-derived duration, and every-node SHA-256/manifests
resources.latency_p50_estimator: conventional median with middle-pair averaging for even sample counts

storage.scope: sum of pg_total_relation_size and pg_indexes_size for every ordinary, materialized-view, and partitioned relation in schema ocpm; database size is reported separately as a diagnostic

Q1.measurement_boundary: fresh Linux process: baseline after connection, provenance query, and one prepared statement; then one PostgreSQL generation/fetch, every OCPB node decode, and complete owned-tree materialization; RSS and VmHWM sampled while the entire tree remains live and before external-ID maps or canonicalization are loaded
Q1.correctness_boundary: after the memory sample, load external-ID maps and require duplicate-preserving canonical JSON SHA-256 and manifest parity for every node, including exact violations and Q6 typed label/child-derived duration
Q1.postgres_backend_memory_scope: non-peak retained-memory diagnostic from sum(total_bytes) in pg_backend_memory_contexts on the same PostgreSQL connection, sampled before and after the candidate request; client VmHWM is the peak-memory gate
